_: THE PARITY RECORD (#2891 S4). doc/design/harness-adapters.md §5.1 makes the
event log the record and gives it TWO projections: the engine's VT renderer
(crates/loomux-engine/src/harness/transcript.rs), which feeds the pane's
OutputBuf ring and with it get_output, termgrid replay, thumbnails,
last_exit_tail and replay-on-attach; and the DOM renderer (src/structuredview.ts
-> src/structuredpane.ts), which is the human's surface. §5.1 states the risk
that shape creates in one line — 'two projections of one log can disagree' — and
assigns the control to the slice that builds the DOM renderer.
WHY THIS IS A TABLE AND NOT AN EQUALITY. The obvious control is 'both
projections draw the same set of kinds', and it is FALSE BY DESIGN: the VT
renderer draws nothing for Thinking or ToolOutput, and has no turn row at all,
and it argues
why in place (volume, and what a thumbnail would then be full of). An equality
assertion would have to be weakened until it caught nothing. So the record is
per-kind, every divergence carries its reason, and BOTH sides assert against
this file: a NEW divergence cannot be added silently, and an existing one
cannot be closed without saying so here.
WHAT 'draws' MEANS ON EACH SIDE, because they are different questions about
the same event. vt: Renderer::render returned a non-empty byte string. dom:
project() changed the State — a block created or updated, or a header/ticker
fact set. Both are 'did this projection show the human anything about this
event', which is the question a divergence is about.
`draws` IS PER KIND, NOT PER EVENT, and it means "at least once over this log".
Two events of one kind can legitimately differ: `TurnStarted`'s whole output is two
newlines and `Renderer::newline` is a no-op at column 0, so whether it draws depends
on what the event before it left behind. Both sides therefore run ONE projection over
the log in order — one `Renderer`, one `State` — rather than a fresh one per event,
which would answer the question with a fact about the instrument.
The subject is session.harness.jsonl beside this file, and both sides read it.
One line is not a HarnessEvent at all — orrerix's own `delivery`, which rides
the same batch tagged distinctly so a harness cannot forge one — so the VT side
skips it and `local_only` is what stops that exemption growing in silence.

turn_started.why: The VT projection has no turn row at all. A turn boundary there is a blank line and nothing else — and only when one is needed, because `Renderer::newline` is a no-op at column 0, so `TurnStarted` emits bytes only where the previous event left the cursor mid-line. Over this log it never does, so it draws nothing. The turn NUMBER is deliberately absent too: it is loomux's own counter (`TurnId`), and printing an internal identity on the human's screen is what that arm refuses. The DOM projection can afford what a byte stream cannot — it draws a labelled rule carrying the turn's receipt (stop reason, cumulative tokens, cost, duration), which is the unit a human scrolls by.

thinking.why: The VT projection draws nothing for Thinking, argued at the arm: #2891 asks for thinking to be QUIETABLE, which a VT stream cannot offer — so the choice is between always showing it and never showing it, and never is what matches every other pane. It would also put the highest-volume thing pi produces into every thumbnail. The DOM projection is where thinking gets its surface, as its own dim, foldable block on the achromatic dye.

tool_output.why: Same argument by volume, plus one about harness parity: a ToolCall line and its ok/failed are what the ring has always shown for a tool on BOTH harnesses, and streaming a tool's bytes into it on pi alone would make the same session look different by harness for no reported difference. The cost is real and is not hidden — a pi tool's streamed output had no human surface at all until this slice, and the DOM projection is that surface: a mono block with its own scroll under the card, capped, with the elided byte count stated.
